Pal. Regt. הובא למנוחות עולמים בבית הקברות הצבאי RAVENNA WAR CEMETERY, איטליה. מיקום הקבר: IV.C.4.
cvEn:
Moshe Malman, son of Hava and Avraham, was born on 8 Menachem-Av 5678 (7 August 1918) in the Volhynia province of Russia. He immigrated to the Land of Israel with his parents in 1925. He studied at the Geula high school in Tel Aviv, where he combined faithfully and wholeheartedly the study of Torah and the practice of its commandments with action. He applied himself to his studies and took part in every sporting and cultural activity, initiating and carrying them out.

At a young age, in 1933, he took an active part in the Haganah, the pre-state Jewish defense organization. In 5696 (1936), when the violent Arab riots broke out, he was appointed to be responsible for the security of the southern neighborhoods of Tel Aviv, Kiryat HaTikva and Shapira. He worked there day and night, organized the residents, built fortifications and saw to their safety.

When the Second World War broke out in 1939, he gave up his civilian life and was fully mobilized into command roles in the Haganah. The dream of his life was the establishment of the State of Israel and a Hebrew army. In 1942, when the Nazi enemy stood at the gates of Egypt, he could not be content with what was happening in the Land of Israel and asked to take part in the war against the Nazis. He was permitted to enlist in the British Army in the Pioneer Corps, and when the Jewish Brigade was formed he was counted among the pillars of the Third Battalion. He was an exemplary soldier and a leader in his company.

On 20 March 1945, he was deputy commander of the attack operations that the Third Battalion carried out in broad daylight against the position at La Guardiagrele. He was directly in command of the supporting weapons, and his work was then described by the operation's commander as successful and decisive. There they met German soldiers face to face and defeated them.

On 23 Nisan 5705 (6 April 1945), about three weeks before the end of the war, he fell in a fierce battle against the Germans and was buried in the military cemetery at Ravenna. He left behind parents, a brother and a sister. His name is commemorated in the book *The Jewish Brigade*, and at the Geula school in Tel Aviv a shield in his name was traditionally awarded to outstanding athletes.

Further details of his British Army service: Moshe Mehlman (Mehlman Moshe), British service number PAL/38412, enlisted in the British Army in 1942. He was posted to the British Infantry Corps (INF.) in the Buffs regiment. His British Army rank was Sergeant (Sgt.). He was later transferred to the 3rd Jewish Battalion, Palestine Regiment. He was laid to rest at the RAVENNA WAR CEMETERY, Italy. Grave location: IV.C.4.
